title: Methods for the Self-integration of Megamolecular Biopolymers on the Drying Air-LC Interface
protocol: Dissolve sacran7 (0.5 g) in pure water (100 mL) by stirring at ~80 °C for more than 12 h.
Cover the container with plastic wrap during dissolution to prevent evaporation.
Cool the sacran solution at ~25 °C to obtain a 0.5 wt% aqueous solution.
Centrifuge the sacran solution to remove impurities (48,400 x g, 4 °C, 1 h, 3 times).
Dissolve xanthan gum in pure water (100 mL) by stirring at ~80 °C for more than 12 h.
Cover the container with plastic wrap during dissolution to prevent evaporation.
Cool the xanthan gum solution at ~25 °C to obtain a 0.5 wt% aqueous solution.
Prepare a 0.5 wt% tubulin solution (1 mL) in Britton-Robinson buffer on ice.
Incubate the tubulin-GpCpp mixture (950 µL tubulin + 50 µL GpCpp) at ~25 °C for 1 day to obtain a stable MT solution.
Prepare a 0.5 wt% DNA solution in Tris-EDTA buffer.
Keep the 0.5 wt% biopolymer sample solutions at 25 °C for drying experiments.
Cut a silicon sheet into an appropriate shape with dimensions of 5-15 mm, 1 mm, and ~20 mm.
Assemble a one-side-open cell using a silicon spacer and two non-modified glass slides.
Fix both sides of the cell with double clips to prevent leakage.
Slowly add each biopolymer solution (100-300 µL) to the cell using a pipette tip with a ~1-mm pore size.
Remove air bubbles from the cells using a syringe needle.
Place the cells in an oven at 60 °C under atmospheric pressure for evaporation.
Adjust polarizers to 45° and 135° for observation under cross-polarized light.
Fix the positions of the light source, polarizers, sample stage, and camera using an optical rail and rod stands.
Place the sample stage between the two polarizers with a distance of ~5 cm between them.
Place the camera ~20 cm from the sample stage to allow focusing.
At given times, place the samples between the polarizers on the stage parallel to the XZ-plane and cover the device with a black curtain.
Photograph the samples through linear crossed polarizers using a digital single-lens reflex camera with a standard zoom lens.
Control the camera settings such as focal distance using computer software.
Collect photographs hourly for 24 hours to evaluate the change in orientational order parameter during drying.
Measure the transmitted light intensity along the centerline in the Z-direction as a gray value using an image processing program.
Plot a graph of the gray value as a function of the distance from the upper open side.
Make microscopic observations with a polarization microscope equipped with a CCD camera.
Keep a first-order retardation plate in the light path during observations.
Control the conditions for the photos using PC software.
